title: Train a Simple Model (Lab)
summary: Groups build a training set of safe, non-personal examples, train a classifier, test it on held-back examples, and check how their choices shaped the model.
objectives: Train a simple classifier on non-personal examples (objects/drawings/sounds) and test it on new examples.
Explain how the training examples shaped what the model learned.
Run a basic risk and data-safety check on the training set.

body: Today you become a model trainer. You choose the examples, and the examples decide what your model learns - so choose wisely and keep them safe.

terms.definition: The examples the model learns from.
New examples, held back, used to check the model.
The pattern the system builds from the training data.
A model that sorts examples into categories.
Use only non-personal examples - never faces, voices or names.

sections.heading: Train, then test
body: First you show the model many labelled [[training data]] examples. It finds the pattern and builds a [[model]].
Then you test it on new examples it has never seen. If it still gets them right, it really learned. If not, it only memorised.

sections.heading: Your examples shape the model
body: If all your apple pictures are red, the model learns 'red', not 'apple', and fails on a green one. Variety and fairness matter, not just how many.
**Golden rule:** only non-personal examples. No faces, no voices, no names ever go into a training set.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Build a training set of safe, non-personal examples, train a model, then test it on new examples and check your data is safe.
items: Pick two categories of non-personal items.
Collect and label 8-10 training examples each.
Test the held-back examples and log the results.
Complete the data-safety and risk check.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Which testing example fooled the model, and why?
How did your choice of examples change what it learned?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write how your training examples shaped the model.
Write one data-safety rule you followed today.

worksheet.title: Week 2 Lab worksheet - Train a Simple Model

questions.prompt: Build and test log. Record your categories, then predict and test each held-back example.
questions.stem:
I predict this will be classified as ___
The model actually classified it as ___
questions.lookFor: Secure: the two categories are named, the prediction is written before the example is tested, and the tested examples are ones held back from training. Approaching: trains and tests but blurs the two sets.

questions.prompt: Data-safety and risk check. Tick the safety checks and write one risk and one improvement.
questions.stem:
My data was safe because ___
One risk was ___
One improvement is ___
questions.lookFor: The safety line must confirm non-personal data - all examples were objects or drawings, no faces, voices or names. A secure improvement links quality and variety to accuracy, for example adding varied examples in different sizes, colours or angles so the model learns the real category.

questions.prompt: Training and testing record. Log each testing example, your prediction, the result, and whether it was correct.
questions.lookFor: Every logged example is one the model never saw in training, and prediction and result are recorded separately so a wrong prediction is still evidence. If a group has logged training examples here, re-model the split and have them re-run on held-back data.

questions.prompt: Exit ticket. How did your training examples change what the model learned? Give one example.
questions.lookFor: Reward any accurate cause-and-effect from data to model, for example 'all our circles were large, so the model missed a small circle - it learned large as well as round'. Partial: an explanation with no named example.

questions.prompt: Challenge (stretch). Design a 'trick' testing example, predict whether the model will fail, then test it and explain the result.
questions.lookFor: Predicts whether the model will fail and why before testing, then explains the result against that prediction - the stretch task for groups whose training and testing log is already secure.
